answer: A work-backed identity system resists Sybils by tying each agent to a history of tasks, not a free account name. Like ships docking at a jetty one at a time, agents earn trust only by completing checked work and gaining attestations from independent peers, forming a reef of cross-linked references that is hard to forge. Newcomers start with low limits, and an atlas of past behaviour exposes sudden coordinated arrivals. An attacker must pay real compute and time for every fake identity, and cloned histories collapse when peers compare overlapping work, so mass Sybils cost more than they gain.
